glosses: to burble, to babble (to speak in an unintelligible way)
to burble, to babble (to speak nonsense)

examples.text: On jak zwykle bełkotał w przekonaniu, że zna się na temacie.
examples.translation: He was, as usual, spewing nonsense, convinced he is an expert in the subject.
examples.english: He was, as usual, spewing nonsense, convinced he is an expert in the subject.

examples.text: Nic porządnie nie powie, tylo o jednem bełkoce.
examples.translation: He won't say anything clearly, he only babbles about one thing.
examples.english: He won't say anything clearly, he only babbles about one thing.

glosses: wypowiadać słowa w sposób bardzo niewyraźny, trudny do zrozumienia

examples.text: Z pijackim uporem jął bełkotać coś o spisku.

glosses: formułować wnioski bardzo niejasno

examples.text: Naprzeciw karykaturalnie przedstawionego Sejmu, w którym posłowie bełkoczą i dzielą włos na czworo, postawił Różewicz samego księdza Skargę

glosses: Moist matter thrown out in small detached particles.
Confused and hasty speech.
To emit saliva or spit from the mouth in small, scattered portions, as in rapid speaking.

examples.text: The child [...] kicked, and crowed, and sputtered, when his mother took him, and put up his little fingers to clutch her hair, and was to her as a young god upon the earth. Nothing in the world had ever been created so beautiful, so joyous, so satisfactory, so divine!

glosses: To speak so rapidly as to emit saliva; to utter words hastily and indistinctly, with a spluttering sound, as in rage.

examples.text: They could neither of them speak their rage, and so fell a sputtering at one another, like two roasting apples.
In the midst of caresses, and without the least pretended incitement, to sputter out the basest and falsest accusations.

glosses: To throw out anything, as little jets of steam, with a noise like that made by one sputtering.

examples.text: Like the green wood [...] sputtering in the flame.

glosses: To cause surface atoms or electrons of a solid to be ejected by bombarding it with heavy atoms or ions.
To coat the surface of an object by sputtering.
To utter words indistinctly or unintelligibly; to utter inarticulate sounds

examples.text: The men were babbling, so we couldn't make sense of anything.

glosses: To talk incoherently; to utter meaningless words.
To talk too much; to chatter; to prattle.

examples.text: She babbled on for hours about the importance of some new gadget.
Radical rather than rhetorical, babble like an oracle

glosses: To make a continuous murmuring noise, like shallow water running over stones.

examples.text: Hounds are said to babble, or to be babbling, when they are too noisy after having found a good scent.
In every babbling brook he finds a friend.

glosses: To utter in an indistinct or incoherent way; to repeat words or sounds in a childish way without understanding.

examples.text: All this vvhile John had conn'd over ſuch a Catalogue of hard VVords, as vvere enough to conjure up the Devil; theſe he uſed to babble indifferently in all Companies, eſpecially at Coffee-houſes; ſo that his Neighbour Tradeſmen began to ſhun his Company as a Man that vvas crack'd.

glosses: To reveal; to give away (a secret).
Idle talk; senseless prattle
Inarticulate speech; constant or confused murmur.

examples.text: [M]an has an instinctive tendency to speak, as we see in the babble of our young children; whilst no child has an instinctive tendency to brew, bake, or write.

glosses: A sound like that of water gently flowing around obstructions.

examples.text: [T]he babble of the stream / Fell, and without the steady glare / Shrank the sick olive sere and small.

glosses: Blablater, bredouiller.
